headline: A CREATOR SERIES COSTS A BRAND 300,000 TO 500,000 DOLLARS FOR 40 PIECES OF CONTENT, THE SAME TEN EPISODES AS UNSCRIPTED TELEVISION COST ABOUT FIVE MILLION IN PRODUCTION ALONE, AND THE BRAND PAYING FOR IT DOES NOT OWN IT
deck: Somebody finally published the price list.  Digiday ran the numbers this morning from a producer who sells brand-funded creator series for a living, and the headline figure makes creator video look like the cheap option.  It is not the cheap option.  It is a different purchase.  For the money you get roughly 40 usable pieces of footage and a licence to put them places.  You do not get the programme.  The creator keeps the majority of that, and you get first refusal on the next run.  Read the two numbers as what they are and the whole argument about funding owned video changes shape.
tldr: A brand-funded creator series of ten long-form episodes plus three short videos each, 40 pieces in total, averages 300,000 to 500,000 dollars against about 5 million for ten episodes of unscripted television in production alone, and the brand does not own the result, with ownership usually splitting 60-40 or 70-30 in the creator's favour.  Write the rights and the asset count into your next series budget above the episode count, and get a signature from every team that is supposed to reuse the footage before you agree the price.

The most expensive election in American history ended last night, 53 percent of the 2.5 billion dollar increase over 2022 went into adverts inside streaming apps on television sets, that spending grew 122 percent to 2.4 billion, and Fox put about 50 million of its own 350 million political take on Tubi alone.  Value your pre-empted spots and the make-goods you are owed today, then ask every streaming seller in a contested market for a rate on the rest of November now that the political buyer has gone.

Sponsored creator posts averaged 334,055 views against 48,008 for gifted posts across 1,755 posts in 20 campaigns, and the gap is mostly the paid media attached to the fee rather than anything about the creator, on a sample that was already selected as the top 75 posts per campaign by engagement.  Demand the paid media spend as a column on every creator performance table you are shown, and work out cost per thousand people reached on your last ten gifted and ten paid posts this week.

JCPenney's longer video on Reddit completed 90 percent better than its shorter one and moved advertising awareness four points, on a single campaign that Reddit itself chose to publish, in the same quarter Reddit launched a 15-second unit on top of its six-second one.  Cut two versions of your next social video from the same footage, around six seconds and around fifteen, run them on the same placement and compare completion rather than views.

WPP's production business grew 2.5 percent last quarter while its creative business shrank 5.1 percent, worse than the 3.5 percent decline the quarter before, and SharkNinja shipped a four-celebrity global holiday campaign the same week with no agency at all.  Split your own pipeline into making and thinking, measure the growth rate of each, and lead every new conversation with whichever half is growing.

Community co-streamers took 63.1 percent of the watch time at the League of Legends world championship group stage across 262 channels, with Caedrel alone taking almost 32 percent of all community viewing, while Kick posted record hours watched and a record channel count and published no average concurrent figure at all.  Ask every event you sponsor for peak, average and hours with the airtime that produced them, divide the hours by the airtime yourself, and price the deal on official channels only until you get the co-stream split in writing.

Mark Denney doubled his median views from 20,011 to 44,725 after narrowing to one subject, locking his runtime into a twelve-minute band and cutting his video descriptions from twelve links to one on 7 October, and he has had no sponsor of any kind for six weeks.  If you sell photo-editing software, filters or tripods, offer him a funded mid-roll inside the tutorial format he is already making, and cut your own video descriptions to one link this week.
